observations: 9.0.0 TeeImpl::Create starts a thread with tee.get() and retains its HANDLE only in a local AutoHandle. TeeImpl has no custom destructor or thread member. The virtual base destructor does not wait for the background thread.

RunSubprocess waits for the process and obtains its exit code, then returns and destroys the Tee without waiting for pending output to drain. The Tee's input/output AutoHandles may close while the thread is using them. This can lose terminal log output without changing the child exit code.

The exact upstream fix retains the thread HANDLE and waits during Tee destruction, then performs bounded synchronous-I/O cancellation when a writer outlives the job. It adds one drain regression and one held-writer timeout regression.

RepoDefinitionFunction checks canonical REPOSITORY_OVERRIDES before its BAZEL_TOOLS embedded_tools fallback. RepositoryFetchFunction routes RepoOverride to setupOverride. This is direct source evidence that --override_repository=bazel_tools=<local-path> can replace the repository through the normal interface.

BUILD.tools selects tools/test/tw.exe for the Windows test_wrapper filegroup. TestActionBuilder obtains the fixed private $test_wrapper prerequisite. No public test_wrapper option was found in the inspected TestConfiguration; this is not an exhaustive negative claim about every Bazel source.
The exact 9.0.0 tw_test.cc contains 18 declared TestWrapperWindowsTest cases; the two upstream additions produce 20 declared cases without changing the existing 18.
recommended_scope: Create a separate research candidate using exact official 9.0.0 source and dependencies with only the two e50 source/test changes; preserve upstream attribution.

Build original //tools/test:tw and //tools/test:tw_test on the actual Windows toolchain, run the complete 18 original plus 2 added tests, and record exact source inputs, commands and output binary digest.

Copy the complete embedded_tools repository into an isolated temporary directory, replace only tools/test/tw.exe, and verify the full file inventory has exactly that one byte change. Keep the installed Bazel original and xml.exe unchanged.

Use the official repository override for the bounded qualification run and prove its effective target/action input selection. Retain the original Rust test body, full target, timeout, no-retry/no-filter rules and exact two-case plus terminal summary checks.
limitations: Static review supports the output-loss mechanism and official override route; it does not prove that this was the sole cause of the specific missing Robrix case.
The upstream bounded destructor does not guarantee complete output from arbitrarily long-lived or uncancellable writers. Strict complete-case/log checks remain required.
No Windows compilation, upstream regression, override execution or product test was run by this reviewer.
The research tool override must be qualified before any default-tool adoption; no production ref was changed by this review.
